symptom: The Draft 2020-12 Shadow Evidence schema constrained trim-canonical scope.runKind/modelVersion and nonblank source.journalMode, but omitted the runtime's absolute-path-token privacy denial for these scalar strings. Synthetic POSIX, drive-letter, UNC, and file-URL tokens passed their schema lexical rules while runtime validation rejected them. No real private paths, odds, databases, or production behavior were accessed.
lesson: A scalar string can satisfy schema type, trim and nonblank rules yet still contain a synthetic local path token. A runtime-only privacy walk does not protect schema-only consumers. Reuse the same lexical path-token rule for scalar and dynamic count-map ingress without weakening HTTPS negative controls.
guardrail: Use a single Draft 2020-12 $defs.pathToken pattern, referenced under not by scope.runKind, scope.modelVersion, source.journalMode and countMap.propertyNames; test POSIX, drive-letter, UNC, file URL, Unicode whitespace and benign HTTPS synthetic controls against runtime validation. Keep digest and semantic checks; lexical parity does not confer provenance, finality or production authority.
